newsitem.title: CANADA: DBRS confirms Quebec ratings with negative trend.
newsitem.headline: DBRS confirms Quebec ratings with negative trend.

text.p: Dominion Bond Rating Service on Tuesday said it confirmed the Province of Quebec's long- and short-term debt ratings with continued negative trends.

The Toronto-based bond rating agency confirmed the long-term rating of Quebec and provincially owned utility Hydro-Quebec at A (low) with a negative trend. The short-term rating was confirmed at R-1 (low) negative, also with a negative trend.

In confirming the province, DBRS said the ratings reflect the province's high level of debt relative to gross domestic product, its slowly growing economy, recently experienced revenue shortfalls and what DBRS calculates to be the largest deficit relative to GDP of any Canadian provinces.

DBRS said the weakness in fiscal indicators was partly mitigated by the province's well diversified economy. The agency also noted that conditions have started to improve as the growth in debt relative to the economy has started to slow, and that the province has taking another step along its deficit elimination plan.

The Quebec government has demonstrated a strong determination to meet its deficit targets, DBRS said. But the agency noted that should revenue shortfalls persist, the government has limited ablility to increase revenues and less flexibility in reducing future program expenditures.
